explanation: Bimodal single-anchor copy head: at each token it either parks on a sink (the passage's first token or a period) and writes ~0, or locks (attention ~1.0) onto one earlier-or-current anchor token and copies it onward over the following function words (and, of, in, the, commas, '?'), so its strength is set by which token is anchored. It is strong (0.45-0.9 of max, highest in long passages) when the anchor is a physical substance or material, food, chemical, drug, body part or disease word (asbestos, nicotine, glucose, rice, wine, coal, copper, cough, tumor), a rare proper-name or brand fragment (Tor of BitTorrent, Guang, Hong, Saskatchewan) or a non-Latin-script piece (Korean, Arabic, Icelandic letters such as ð/Ö), moderate (0.3-0.45) on everyday concrete objects (car, bus, engine, river, dog), and stays at ~0 for whole clauses built only from pronouns, person and role nouns (man, king, teacher, doctor, friend, mother), abstract nouns (idea, story, love, answer), weekdays or spelled numbers, and in Cyrillic text and short code.
